'''Takeiwatatsu no Mikoto''' (健磐龍命; {{nihongo||たけいわたつのみこと}}; born 14 years before Emperor Jimmu's accession<ref name="gunshi"/> — died 15th day of the 8th month, Hinoe-Uma year of Emperor Jimmu's 93rd year<ref name="gunshi"/>) was an ancient Japanese figure or deity. There is a theory that he is identical with '''Asotsuhi ko no Mikoto'''{{Refnest|group="note"|Also written Asotsuhi ko,<ref name="syoki">''[[Nihon Shoki]]'', chapter on [[Emperor Keikō]].</ref> Asotsuhi ko no Mikoto,<ref name="ruien"/> and Aso Tsuhiko no Mikoto.<ref name="ruien"/>}} (あそつひこのみこと), who appears in the Keikōki section of the ''[[Nihon Shoki]]''.<ref name="ruien"/>

He is now known as the principal deity of [[Aso Shrine]]<ref>"Takeiwatatsu no Mikoto." ''Nihon Jinmei Daijiten'', Kōdansha.</ref> and bears the divine titles Takeiwatatsu no Mikoto no Kami,<ref name="shiki"/> Takeiwatatsu no Kami,<ref name="ruien"/> '''Aso no Kami''',<ref name="ruien"/> Aso Ōkami,<ref name="gunshi"/> and '''Aso Daimyōjin'''.<ref name="saijin">[http://www.aso-dm.net/?阿蘇神社の祭神%28さいじん%29について About the deities of Aso Shrine] — Asopedia (accessed 25 July 2018 16:55 JST).</ref> He later also took on the character of a volcanic deity of [[Mount Aso]].

== Genealogy ==
There are five theories regarding Takeiwatatsu no Mikoto's lineage.

The '''first''' holds that he was the fifth child of '''[[Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]]'''.<ref name="gunshi"/><ref name="ruien"/> Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto was the third imperial prince of [[Emperor Jimmu]] (the first [[Emperor of Japan|Emperor]]) and elder brother of [[Emperor Suizei]] (the second Emperor); according to tradition he yielded the throne to his younger brother and dedicated himself to the service of the gods.<ref>''[[Nihon Shoki]]''.</ref>

The '''second''' holds that he was the sixth child of Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto.<ref name="gunshi"/>

The '''third''' holds that he was the grandson of Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto.<ref>''[[Sendai Kuji Hongi]]'', "Kokuzo Hongi."</ref>

The '''fourth''' holds that he was the fifth-generation descendant of Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto.<ref name="gunshi"/>

The '''fifth''' holds that he was the eleventh-generation descendant of Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto.<ref>Suwa clan genealogy, supplement, p. 13.</ref>

* '''Legal wife'''<ref name="sosyo">''Suwa Shiryō Sōsho'', vol. 28.</ref>: '''Asobime no Mikoto'''<ref name="ihon"/> (also Asotsu Hime no Mikoto<ref name="gunshi"/><ref name="ruien"/> (あそつひめ<ref name="kou"/>)){{Refnest|group="note"|Also written Asotsu Hime,<ref name="ruien"/> Aso Tsuhime,<ref name="ruien"/> Aso Hime,<ref name="ruien"/> Aso Hime no Kami,<ref name="sosyo"/> Asobime no Mikoto,<ref name="ruien"/> Asobime no Kami,<ref name="ruien"/> Asobime,<ref name="ruien"/> Asotsu Hime no Kami,<ref name="gunshi"/> and Hime no Kami.<ref name="ruien"/>}}
*: Second deity of Aso Shrine. Daughter of [[Kusabe Yoshimi no Kami (Kusakuni no Kami)|Kusabe Yoshimi no Kami (Kuniryu no Kami)]]{{Refnest|group="note"|A prince who remained in [[Hyūga Province|Hyūga]] during the [[Jimmu's eastern campaign|Eastern Campaign]] of Emperor Jimmu to guard the rear, and later moved to Kusabe. The place name "Kusabe" is said to derive from Yoshimi no Kami having used grass as temporary walls and roof for a residence; it later became "Kusabe" (草部).<ref name="gunshi"/> According to the ''[[Kojiki]]'', this deity was the elder brother of [[Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] — the father of Takeiwatatsu no Mikoto — making Asobime no Mikoto an uncle-niece relationship with Takeiwatatsu no Mikoto by one reckoning (the ''Nihon Shoki'' does not mention this). That is, Asobime no Mikoto and Takeiwatatsu no Mikoto were cousins, making this a cousin marriage.}}<ref name="ruien"/>
** First child<ref>[http://www.aso-dm.net/?国造神社 Kokuzo Shrine] — Asopedia (accessed 25 July 2018 16:00 JST).</ref>: '''[[Hayamikatama no Mikoto]]'''<ref name="keizu"/> (はやみかたまのみこと / はやかめたまのみこと<ref name="ruien"/>; also Hayamikadama no Mikoto<ref name="keizu"/>)
**: Deity of [[Kokuzo Shrine]]. According to the "Kokuzo Hongi" in the ''[[Sendai Kuji Hongi]]'', he was appointed the first [[Aso Kokuzo]] during the reign of [[Emperor Sujin]] (the tenth Emperor). Ancestor of the Aso clan.<ref name="keizu"/>
*** Grandson: '''[[Takenumi no Mikoto]]'''<ref name="seishi1">''Seishi Keikei Daijiten'', vol. 1.</ref>{{Refnest|group="note"|Also written Korehito no Mikoto,<ref name="seishi1"/> Korehito no Mikoto, Korehito no Kimi no Mikoto,<ref name="kou"/> Korehito,<ref name="ruien"/> Hikomikoakari,<ref name="seishi1"/> Hikomikoakari Myōjin,<ref name="gunshi"/> Yaibimimitama no Mikoto,<ref name="seishi1"/> and Yaibi Mimi no Mikoto.<ref name="saijin"/>}}
***: Deity of [[Kōsa Shrine]]. Also said to be a child of Takeiwatatsu no Mikoto. First of the Grand Priests (Guji).<ref name="gunshi"/>
*** Grandson: [[Takahashi no Kami]]<ref name="ricchi">[http://www.aso-dm.net/?阿蘇神社の立地 Location of Aso Shrine] — Asopedia (accessed 25 July 2018 20:54 JST).</ref>
***: Deity of [[Ryōjinja]] ([[Oguni, Kumamoto|Oguni Town]]). Second child of Hayamikatama no Mikoto.
*** Grandson: [[Himiya no Kami]] (also Hi no Miya no Kami)<ref name="ricchi"/>
***: Deity of Ryōjinja. Third child of Hayamikatama no Mikoto.

== Historical records ==
The following presents records of Takeiwatatsu no Mikoto by source.

=== Nihon Shoki ===
The ''[[Nihon Shoki]]'' contains the following account of Asotsuhi ko. On the 16th day of the 6th month of the 18th year of [[Emperor Keikō]]'s reign, the Emperor arrived in Aso Province as part of his [[Emperor Keikō#Kyushu campaign|Kyushu tour]]. The land was wide and open and no people could be seen. The Emperor said: "Are there people in this land?" At that moment, '''Asotsuhi ko''' and '''Asotsuhi me''', two deities, suddenly took human form and came before the Emperor, saying: "We two are here. How could there be no people?" For this reason the land was named '''[[Aso Province|Aso]]'''. It should be noted, however, that the ''Nihon Shoki'' contains no record identifying Asotsuhi ko with Takeiwatatsu no Mikoto.

=== Fudoki of Higo Province ===
The ''[[Higo Province Fudoki]]'' contains nearly the same account as the ''Nihon Shoki''. Emperor Keikō's words are identical, but the two deities' reply reads: "We two deities — Asotsuhi ko and Asotsuhi me — are here now in this land. How could there be no people?"

=== Engishiki ===
The ''[[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]'' lists "Takeiwatatsu no Mikoto Shrine" (たけいわたつのみことの-) as a [[meishin taisha|great shrine of celebrated deities]] (Meijin Taisha) in [[Aso District, Kumamoto|Aso District]], [[Higo Province]]. Today '''[[Aso Shrine]]''' — the chief shrine of Aso — enshrines Takeiwatatsu no Mikoto as its first deity.<ref name="ruien"/>

The founding of Aso Shrine is attributed to the 9th year of [[Emperor Kōrei]]'s reign, in the 6th month, when Emperor Kōrei (the seventh Emperor) ordered '''[[Hayamikatama no Mikoto]]'''<ref name="keizu"/> (mentioned above) to enshrine Takeiwatatsu no Mikoto as a deity.<ref name="gunshi"/> It is also said that on the 26th day of that month the Emperor ordered the reconstruction of the Aso Shrine building.<ref name="gunshi"/>

Another account holds that Aso Shrine was built at Miyaji Village upon Emperor Keikō's visit to Aso (described above) when he commanded Hayamikatama no Mikoto to build it. A further account states that in the 18th year of Emperor Keikō's reign, the Emperor ordered '''[[Takenumi no Mikoto]]''' (mentioned above) to show especial veneration to Aso Shrine.<ref name="gunshi"/>

=== Kokuzo Hongi ===
According to the "Kokuzo Hongi" in the ''[[Sendai Kuji Hongi]]'', during the reign of [[Emperor Sujin]] (the tenth [[Emperor of Japan|Emperor]]), '''[[Hayamikatama no Mikoto]]''' — who shared a common ancestor with the [[Hi no Kokuzo|Hino Kokuzo]] and was the grandson of '''[[Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' (son of [[Emperor Jimmu]], the first Emperor) — was appointed the first [[Aso Kokuzo]]. Hayamikatama no Mikoto also carried forward the will of his father '''Takeiwatatsu no Mikoto''' in spreading agriculture and working to advance animal husbandry and forestry.<ref name="kokuzou">[http://www.aso-dm.net/?国造神社 Kokuzo Shrine] — Asopedia (accessed 25 July 2018 16:00 JST).</ref>

=== Traditions of Aso ===
The following presents traditions based primarily on the ''[[#gunshi|Aso County Gazetteer]]'' (阿蘇郡誌).

Takeiwatatsu no Mikoto was born in the 14th year before Emperor Jimmu's accession as the fifth child of [[Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]].

In the 76th year of Emperor Jimmu's reign, the Emperor issued an order to his grandson Takeiwatatsu no Mikoto to pacify the western seas (Saikaido) and bestowed upon him the territory of Hino-Kuni. In the 2nd month of that year, Takeiwatatsu no Mikoto descended from [[Uji no Sato|Uji Village]] in [[Yamashiro Province]] to Aso. During the journey, he enshrined the spirit of Emperor Jimmu at the site of the Emperor's former palace in [[Miyazaki]], which is said to be the founding of [[Miyazaki Jingu]].<ref name="jingu"/> From there he moved to [[Nobeoka]], then traveled upstream along the [[Gokase River]] and stayed for a time at the foot of [[Ontake, Kumamoto|Mitake Mountain]], passing through places such as Narikimi, Sakatsuba, and Murasame-zaka.<ref name="yoshimi">[http://www.aso-dm.net/?草部吉見神%28くさかべよしみのかみ%29とその娘の阿蘇都媛%28あそつひめ%29 Kusabe Yoshimi no Kami and his daughter Aso Tsuhime] — Asopedia (accessed 25 July 2018 21:49 JST).</ref> Then from Mitake he entered [[Mabaru]] and erected the [[Heitate Shrine|Heitate Palace]] to worship the heavenly and earthly deities.<ref name="yoshimi"/> From there he moved to Kusabe, took '''[[Asotsuhi me|Aso Tsuhime]]''' (mentioned above) as his wife, assumed the name Asotsuhi ko, and then moved to Aso.

At the time, the interior of the [[Aso Caldera]] — [[Aso Valley|Aso Valley]] and [[Nango Valley|Nango Valley]] — was a lake (called "[[Kaitori Lake|Kaitori Lake]]"). Takeiwatatsu no Mikoto sought to drain the lake to create farmland.

During this time a child was born, and for this reason the place came to be called [[Ubuyama, Kumamoto|Ubuyama]] ("mountain where birth occurred").<ref>[http://www.aso-dm.net/?健磐龍命 Takeiwatatsu no Mikoto] — Asopedia (accessed 25 July 2018 21:04 JST).</ref> Another account says the one born was Takeiwatatsu no Mikoto's eldest grandchild, and the name means "the place where a mountain was born" in the sense of comparing the lord to a mountain.<ref name="mura"/> Yet another account says it was Aso Ōkami himself who was born there.

After moving on, Takeiwatatsu no Mikoto attempted to kick through the outer rim of the caldera to drain the water, but the pass was double-layered and could not be broken through ([[Futae Pass|Futae-tōge]]). On a second attempt he found a gap in the mountain and succeeded, and the lake water flowed out to the west. The word for "there is a gap" was contracted to "sugaru," and from then on that place was called "Sugaru Falls." The modern writing "Sugaru Falls" (数鹿流ヶ滝) is said to derive from several deer (数匹の鹿) being swept away.<ref name="kako">[http://www.aso-dm.net/?立野火口瀬 Tateno Crater Gorge] — Asopedia (accessed 25 July 2018 20:04 JST).</ref> Also, when Takeiwatatsu no Mikoto kicked through the mountain he fell on his back (sitting down) and said "I cannot stand" (立てぬ), which is said to be the origin of the place name [[Tateno, Kumamoto|Tateno]].<ref name="kako"/>

The small hills and Toshima in [[Kumamoto City]] are said to be fragments of the kicked-through mountain; [[Kikuyō, Kumamoto|Tsukure]] in [[Kikuyo Town]] is said to be an abbreviation of "tsuchikure" (土塊, clod of earth) for the place where lumps of earth fell; and the place name [[Kōshi, Kumamoto|Kōshi]] (合志) is said to derive from small stones. [[Ōzu, Kumamoto|Hikimizu]] in Ōtsu Town is another place name connected to this legend.

There is also a tradition that Takeiwatatsu no Mikoto slew a great catfish that had been blocking the flow of water.<ref>[http://www.aso-dm.net/?阿蘇をひらいた神の健磐龍命(たけいわたつのみこと) The deity who opened Aso — Takeiwatatsu no Mikoto] — Asopedia (accessed 25 July 2018 19:30 JST).</ref>

It is a geological fact that the interior of the Aso Caldera was once a lake and disappeared as a result of a breach near Tateno; the estimated date of the breach is earlier than 73,000 years ago.<ref name="karudera">[http://www.aso-dm.net/?カルデラ湖 Caldera lake] — Asopedia (accessed 25 July 2018 17:30 JST).</ref> In the northern part of the caldera, paddles from the [[Yayoi period]] have been excavated, indicating that part of the area remained a water zone until quite recently.<ref name="karudera"/>

After this, Takeiwatatsu no Mikoto shot an arrow himself and established his palace at the place where it fell. This is the site of the present [[Aso Shrine#Yamura-sha|Yamura-sha]]. The place name [[Miyaji, Aso|Miyaji]] ("palace site") derives from where he established this palace. Near this palace, settlements called "Imamura," "Nishimura," and "Nishimachi" are said to have formed.<ref>[http://www.aso-dm.net/?矢村社%28やむらしゃ%29と矢島%28やしま%29、振石%28ふりいし%29が谷%28たに%29 Yamura-sha, Yashima, and Furiishi Valley] — Asopedia (accessed 25 July 2018 19:55 JST).</ref><ref>[http://www.aso-dm.net/?矢村社 Yamura-sha] — Asopedia (accessed 25 July 2018 19:55 JST).</ref> After this, Takeiwatatsu no Mikoto pacified the remaining unruly elements of the region.

Takeiwatatsu no Mikoto governed the Aso region and died at the age of 107 on the 15th day of the 8th month, Hinoe-Uma year of Emperor Jimmu's 93rd year. In front of the tower gate of [[Aso Shrine]] in [[Aso City]] there is a divine mound (shinryō): among two small hills, the northern is said to be the mound of Takeiwatatsu no Mikoto and the southern that of Aso Tsuhime no Kami.

=== Other ===
* Takeiwatatsu no Mikoto was said to have been the "Governor of Kyushu."<ref name="jingu"/>
* Emperor Jimmu is said to have bestowed Aso upon Takeiwatatsu no Mikoto on the 1st day of the 2nd month of Emperor Jimmu's 76th year.<ref name="ruien"/>
* Takeiwatatsu no Mikoto is said to have descended from [[Yamato Province]] to Aso in the 2nd month of Emperor Jimmu's 76th year.<ref name="ruien"/>
* The later Grand Priest family (Guji) of [[Aso Shrine]] — descendants of Takeiwatatsu no Mikoto — being the [[Uji clan|Uji clan]] is said to derive from the fact that Takeiwatatsu no Mikoto departed from [[Uji no Sato|Uji]].<ref name="ruien"/>

== Sites of legend ==
* [[Aso Ōmikami Goashiato-ishi]] (Shirakawa Nishi-yanagi, [[Minami-Aso, Kumamoto|Minami-Aso Village]])
*: A large boulder at Shirakawa Kenuya-dō said to bear the footprint of Takeiwatatsu no Mikoto.<ref name="ashi">[http://www.aso-dm.net/?阿蘇大御神御足跡石 Aso Daimyōjin Goashiato-ishi] — Asopedia (accessed 25 July 2018 20:44 JST).</ref> Only the tradition survived while the stone itself had been lost, but in 1999 (Heisei 11) it was rediscovered by local residents.<ref name="ashi"/>
